abstract: Accurate modelling of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) coils requires coil-specific geometric and electrical parameters. Yet detailed manufacturer models are rarely available, and internals may be widely available to companies in the field but not to researchers. The development of new coils should ideally build on all existing prior art. This work presents a technology benchmark and modelling-ready dataset for seventeen widely used commercial TMS coils across multiple manufacturers and geometries. High-resolution micro-CT (0.0495 mm resolution, material and density contrast) serves to reconstruct winding and casing structures and to extract parameters directly usable in numerical models, including loop dimensions, conductor cross-section, turn count, winding height, and winding-to-surface (casing) thickness. Complementary electrical measurements provide spectral impedance (series resistance and inductance) scans from 20 Hz to 200 kHz, together with dc resistance. In addition to baseline geometry and impedance, the study documents practical construction features relevant to safety and usability with detailed insights into their internal construction (e.g., cooling architectures and embedded sensing). The resulting benchmark dataset supports coil-specific electric-field simulations, reduces modelling uncertainty associated with generic assumptions (e.g., fixed coil-scalp spacing), and provides a quantitative reference for designing and evaluating new coil technologies against established commercial solutions. As a simulation-readiness example, we generated a calibrated CT-derived MCB70 line-current model for SimNIBS and evaluated its effect on predicted electric-field metrics. Compared with the SimNIBS MCB70 model, the CT-derived model produced measurable differences under identical placement conditions. We provide the dataset online.
